Hi Emily — happy to jump in with some of the technical cost levers. High-level notes: 

- Per-token hosted: you pay per generated/input token. Cost scales linearly with token volume. Good for variable/low commit workloads and fastest time-to-value. Latency is low for small batch sizes, but unit cost is higher than amortized dedicated capacity.

- Dedicated reserved commits: you reserve GPU capacity (monthly commit) and pay a lower per-token effective rate when fully utilized. Main drivers: utilization (how much of the reserved capacity you use), sequence length (longer sequences increase compute), and concurrency (affects batching efficiency).

- Private/VPC or on-prem: procurement includes a platform license + potential one-time setup fee and customer's infra/OPEX. Unit cost can be similar to Dedicated at high utilization, but includes additional procurement lead time and ops overhead. Private is preferred when data residency/compliance or air-gapped requirements exist.

Questions that materially change numbers:
1) Peak concurrent requests and SLA latency targets (p95 target?)
2) Typical response tokens per request vs prompt tokens (you mentioned ~1,200 total but if it's 1,200 response tokens that's heavier)
3) Any requirements for long-term KV cache or stateful sessions that reduce token count but increase memory footprint per request

I've prefilled the spreadsheet with a few scenarios (100%/75%/50% utilization) and a quick Hosted vs Dedicated cost run for 500M tokens/mo. See column notes.

If procurement wants a side-by-side number to show to finance, happy to produce a one-page summary for each option.

—Aditya

Quick answers ahead of the call so procurement/finance have something to look at:

High-level indicative numbers for 500M tokens/mo (illustrative, final depends on utilization and sequence profile):

- Hosted (per-token): ~$0.0008 per input/generated token -> ~ $400k/month at 500M tokens. Pros: no commit, fastest onboarding. Cons: higher unit cost and less predictability.

- Dedicated (reserved capacity): Monthly reserved commit equivalent to 1-2 top-end GPUs for this workload (depends on batch/latency). Typical committed spend range: $90k–$150k/month. Effective per-token when at 75–90% utilization: ~$0.00018–$0.00030 per token. Pros: lower unit cost and predictable billing. Cons: commit required; scale/burst considerations.

- Private (VPC/on-prem): Platform license + deployment services + infra. Indicative: $250k–$400k upfront/first-year (license + setup) + infra/OPEX ongoing (varies). Procurement lead time typically 6–10 weeks for contracts and deployment scheduling. Pros: full data control and compliance. Cons: longer procurement and ops responsibility.

Attachments: I updated acme_cost_model_500M_tokens.xlsx with a 3-scenario sheet (Hosted, Dedicated @ 75% util, Dedicated @ 90% util) and a one-page summary PDF for procurement.
